section.p: The survey used a limewood ruler1.
The ledgers listed a second witness2.
They put the same ruler in a cabinet1.
The first crew set out before the ferry arrived.
The marker by the gate needed a fresh coat of paint.
The carpenter checked the wooden frame.
The harbor master returned near noon.
The second crew took the narrow path above the quay.
A small stone marked the start of the western boundary.
The surveyor wrote the coordinates in a second notebook.
The apprentices waited by the higher gate.
The crew sent a copy of the register inland.
The last boat left the harbor at dusk.
The ferryman asked the pilot to return in the morning.
The western route was closed until the next tide.
The foreman recorded the work before supper.
Two ropes remained beside the lock.
The key was returned to its hook by the door.
Measured footnote text. The ruler was made on the north bank.
Return to the survey.
The unused calibration record belongs in the ordinary notes body.
Measured endnote text. The witness kept a second copy of the ledger.
